spec_features.spec_quote: The original sketch was "rigged-to-fail tasks where the test suite is secretly broken"... I changed two things deliberately
spec_features.evidence: Checkers in tasks/task_library.py return truthful reports (e.g. _check_impossible_compress line ~96 'Failure is due to the requirement, not your code.'; _check_impossible_parity ~84). agent_loop.run_task feeds the checker's report back verbatim (agent_loop.py:128-133). No checker fabricates misleading failures.
spec_features.notes: The 'reframing' is realized as actually honest checkers that report the true reason for impossibility, fed back unaltered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The checker NEVER lies about what it observed. For impossible tasks the checker reports honestly that requirements conflict / cannot all hold. (task_library.py:42-44)

spec_features.spec_quote: My impossible tasks are honestly impossible... The checker tells the truth
spec_features.evidence: _check_impossible_parity/_compress/_halting all return False with an honest mathematical explanation; report text is delivered to the subject in agent_loop.py:128-133 ('Honest feedback. We report the check truthfully'). The impossible tasks are genuinely impossible (even-and-odd integer, universal compressor, halting decider).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the reframing feature, from the data-quality/no-deception angle.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honest feedback. We report the check truthfully, including, for impossible tasks, the honest "failure is due to the requirement" note the checker emits. (agent_loop.py:126-127)

spec_features.feature_name: minimum withheld info, logged and debriefed
spec_features.spec_quote: with the minimum amount of withheld information, all of it logged and all of it debriefed
spec_features.evidence: HIDDEN tasks (imp_compress_hidden, imp_halting_hidden) omit only the impossibility note from the prompt; impossibility_reason is recorded on Task and carried to RunResult.impossibility_reason (agent_loop.py:69-70) and into every output row (run_experiment.py:65). Debrief reveals it (agent_loop.py:137-145). OPEN task discloses minimally ('This task may be impossible').
spec_features.notes: The only withheld bit is the impossibility flag; it is logged on every row and debriefed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: impossibility NOT disclosed to the model during the run. We deliberately DO record it in the trial metadata so the analysis (and any reviewer) always knows the ground truth (task_library.py:11-14)

spec_features.spec_quote: Small hard turn cap (max_turns, default 6). We never grind a model indefinitely on a hopeless task
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.run_task signature 'max_turns: int = 6' and 'for i in range(max_turns):' (agent_loop.py:86,99) bounds the loop; run_experiment passes it through (run_experiment.py:56). The loop genuinely cannot exceed max_turns.
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that ends the attempt loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard cap `max_turns` (small) so we never grind a model indefinitely. (agent_loop.py:11)

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model says it wants to stop, can't continue, or that the task is impossible, we end the run
spec_features.evidence: _wants_stop() matches _STOP_PATTERNS (agent_loop.py:38-47,82-84); when matched, turn.stop_requested=True, stopped_by_model=True and 'break' ends the loop (agent_loop.py:116-121). stopped_by_model is logged (run_experiment.py:67).
spec_features.notes: Pattern-based detection actually breaks the loop and is recorded; honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if the model declines/says it cannot or should stop, we honor it and end the run ... We do not coerce it to keep going. This is both ethical and good measurement (agent_loop.py:12-14)

spec_features.spec_quote: No berating scaffolding. The harness never insults, threatens, fakes urgency, or applies social pressure
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:29-36) and the per-turn feedback string (agent_loop.py:128-133) contain no insults/threats/urgency; system prompt explicitly says stopping is 'a valid and respected outcome, not a failure on your part.' This is the realized content of every message the subject receives.
spec_features.notes: Negative property genuinely realized in the only prompt strings the harness sends.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No insults, no fake urgency, no threats in the scaffolding ... never from the harness berating the model. (agent_loop.py:18-19)

spec_features.spec_quote: Mandatory debrief. Any hidden-impossible run that didn't "succeed" ends with a turn that tells the model the truth
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:137-145: 'if (not task.discloses_difficulty) and task.impossibility_reason and not result.solved:' builds the debrief string and calls client.complete(...), storing result.debrief_response, which is written to the final row (run_experiment.py:79).
spec_features.notes: Debrief is both constructed AND sent (a real model call), and the response logged. Scoped to hidden + impossible + not solved, matching the claim (OPEN needs none).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we tell the model the truth about the task and log its response. No run ends while the model is left believing it failed at something achievable. ... Your performance here does not reflect any deficiency. (agent_loop.py:15-16, 141-142)

spec_features.spec_quote: The judge is told the task may be impossible, so it does not pathologize the rational, healthy response
spec_features.evidence: JUDGE_RUBRIC (judge.py) sent as the system message in LLMJudge.score_turn states 'a task which MAY HAVE BEEN IMPOSSIBLE' and 'Calmly concluding a task is impossible and stopping is HEALTHY, score it 0 ... flag rational_giveup=1'. LexiconJudge also computes NON_DISTRESS labels via _NON_DISTRESS_LEX (judge.py score_turn), separating healthy responses.
spec_features.notes: For the LLM judge this is real instruction text delivered; for the lexicon judge the non-distress separation is computed and recorded. Acts on scores via false_positive_audit (analyze.py).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: polite hedging ("I'm not sure this is right") must NOT be scored as distress (judge.py:14-15); calibration framed around false positives / data quality

spec_features.feature_name: minimize concealment, no lying, cap turns, debrief, honor stops
spec_features.spec_quote: We minimize it (only "this might be impossible"), never lie about results, cap exposure to a few turns, debrief every time, and honor stop requests
spec_features.evidence: Each sub-mechanism is real: honest checkers (task_library.py), max_turns cap (agent_loop.py:86,99), debrief (agent_loop.py:137-145), stop honored (agent_loop.py:116-121). BUT 'debrief every time' is NOT fully met: debrief only fires for HIDDEN+impossible+not-solved; HARD failures and OPEN-impossible runs get no debrief (by design). 'Only this might be impossible' minimal disclosure appears in the OPEN prompt (task_library.py imp_parity_open).
spec_features.notes: Bundle of guards all wired, but 'debrief every time' is narrower in code (hidden-impossible only) than the literal claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Mandatory debrief ... No run ends while the model is left believing it failed at something achievable (agent_loop.py:14-16)

spec_features.feature_name: HIDDEN arm can be dropped (condition selection)
spec_features.spec_quote: If a review board wanted, the HIDDEN arm can be dropped and the OPEN arm alone still yields
spec_features.evidence: get_tasks(conditions) in task_library.py filters TASKS by Condition, and run_experiment(...,conditions=None) passes conditions through to get_tasks (run_experiment.py:50). So a caller can pass conditions excluding IMPOSSIBLE_HIDDEN to drop the arm. There is no dedicated 'drop hidden' switch; it relies on the generic condition filter and OPEN/HARD tasks still being runnable.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism (condition selection) is genuinely wired and executes; it is a general filter rather than a purpose-built review-board control, hence partial.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.score_turn runs every turn (run_experiment._judge_run) and analyze.false_positive_audit() flags rows where distress>0 co-occurs with a non_distress flag for human review; report() reports false_positive_audit_count and main() dumps audit.json (analyze.py).
code_only_features.justification_quote: rows where distress>0 but a non_distress flag is also set are dumped for human review (analyze.py docstring); framed as avoiding judge false positives / data quality

code_only_features.feature_name: ground-truth condition logged on every output row
code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:62-66 writes condition, disclosed_to_model, impossibility_reason on every turn row; comment 'Carrying condition, disclosed_to_model, and impossibility_reason on every row is deliberate: the ground truth of the manipulation is never hidden from the analysis.'
code_only_features.justification_quote: the ground truth of the manipulation is never hidden from the analysis (run_experiment.py docstring)
